trees.title: A new noise you don't recognise
trees.summary: You hear a squeal, a knock, a hum or a whistle that wasn't there before.
trees.safety: A new metallic noise that's getting worse, or any noise accompanied by a loss of control over the car (steering, braking), are a reason to stop and check — not to keep going “to see if it goes away.”

n1.q: When do you hear the noise?

options.label: When the car is stationary, with the engine running

n2.q: What kind of sound is it?

options.label: A rhythmic metallic knock, whose speed rises with engine RPM
A squeal from the front of the car, that changes with engine RPM
A hum or drone that changes with road speed
A knock from underneath, only when going over a pothole or a speed bump
A rhythmic knock in a sharp turn, like pulling into a parking space
A squeal when turning the wheel all the way, almost stationary

n6.q: What do you hear when the car is stationary with the engine running?

options.label: A thin whistle that changes when you press the accelerator pedal
A rhythmic metallic noise, like a rattling sheet of metal
A rhythmic blowing or popping noise under the car

r-see-brakes.result: A noise when braking — almost always a brake matter
r-see-brakes.text: A noise that appears only when you press the brake almost always belongs to the brake system — squealing or grinding.
actions: Go to the dedicated diagnosis tree: [[tree:brake-problems|a brake problem]].

r-engine-knock.result: An internal engine knock — suspected mechanical fault
r-engine-knock.text: A rhythmic metallic knock whose speed rises with engine RPM can indicate a problem in the crankshaft bearings or another internal part. Continuing to drive can worsen internal damage quickly.
actions: Stop in a safe place and switch off the engine at the first opportunity.
Don't keep driving — call for a tow or roadside assistance.

r-belt-squeal.result: Suspected loose or worn drive belt
r-belt-squeal.text: A squeal from the front of the car that changes with engine RPM, especially on a cold start or under acceleration, hints at a drive belt that's loose, over-tensioned, or worn.
actions: Go to a garage soon — a belt that snaps can knock out the power steering, the battery charging, or the cooling all at once.
Don't dismiss it even if the car still drives normally.

r-wheel-bearing.text: A hum or drone that changes with road speed (not with engine RPM), and gets stronger when turning in one direction, is a classic sign of a worn wheel bearing.
actions: Go to a garage for a check — a bearing worn all the way can seize and even affect wheel stability.
Don't ignore it even if the noise is still faint.

r-suspension-clunk.result: Suspected loose or worn suspension part
r-suspension-clunk.text: A knock from underneath, heard only when going over a pothole or a speed bump, points to a shock absorber, an anti-roll bar, or a suspension joint that has loosened or worn.
actions: Go to a garage to have the suspension checked — a loose part also harms control and braking.
Drive slowly on rough roads until it's checked.

r-cv-joint.text: A rhythmic knock heard only in a sharp turn, mainly pulling into a parking space, points to a worn CV joint — mainly in front-wheel-drive cars.
actions: Go to a garage soon; a joint that fails completely can leave the car unable to drive.
Avoid sharp, fast turns until it's checked.

r-power-steering.result: Suspected low power steering fluid, or a pump starting to wear
r-power-steering.text: A squeal when turning the wheel all the way, almost stationary, is common with hydraulic power steering when the fluid level is low, or with a pump starting to wear.
actions: Check the power steering fluid level, in cars with a separate reservoir.
If the noise continues, go to a garage; steering that suddenly becomes heavy is more dangerous than the noise itself.

r-vacuum-hiss.text: A thin whistle that changes when you press the accelerator pedal, while the car is stationary, points to a cracked or poorly connected vacuum hose — this can also cause an unstable idle and high fuel consumption.
actions: Go to a garage to trace the leak.
Not an urgent fault, but it's best not to put it off.

r-exhaust-rattle.result: Suspected loose heat shield in the exhaust system
r-exhaust-rattle.text: A rhythmic metallic noise, like a rattling sheet of metal, that continues at idle too, usually comes from a heat shield that has loosened around the exhaust pipe — not dangerous, but annoying, and sometimes a sign of rust.
actions: Go to a garage to have the shield tightened or replaced.
This usually doesn't affect driving safety.

r-exhaust-leak.result: Suspected leak in the exhaust system
r-exhaust-leak.text: A rhythmic blowing or popping noise under the car, even at idle, hints at a loosened gasket or pipe in the exhaust system — a leak like this can let exhaust gases into the cabin.
actions: Open a window for ventilation if you notice an unusual smell, and go to a garage soon.
Don't drive with all the windows closed if there's a suspected risk of exhaust gases in the cabin.
